g.text: GQA - Grouped-Query Attention: g Q heads share each K/V head
Explained on: session 05 GQA · see also session 02 (memory math), mqa.excalidraw, Beyond → SOTA map (H_kv = H_Q / 4 worked example)
M_KV = 2 . L . B . T . H_kv . d_h . S GQA: 1 < H_kv < H_q, group size g = H_q / H_kv (Ainslie et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.13245)
1 The spectrum: MHA (32) -> 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> MQA (1) (H_q = 32 in every row)
Toy config: L=32, d_h=64, FP16 (S=2), T=100K, B=1; AI = H_q/H_kv
variant H_kv g KiB/tok 100K ctx +14 GB wts AI
KiB/tok = 2 . 32 layers . H_kv . 64 . 2 B = 8 KiB x H_kv
GQA is one dial. H_kv = H_q gives MHA, H_kv = 1 gives MQA.
Each halving of H_kv halves the cache (and the bytes read per token).
There is no universal optimum: quality <-> KV memory <-> bandwidth <-> latency
(an architecture-search problem). Pick g from the budget, not from theory.
2 Group wiring for GQA-8: 4 Q heads -> 1 K/V head
(KV3 .. KV7 omitted) 8 groups x 4 Q heads = 32
Group 1 up close: Q1..Q4 all read the SAME KV1, with different attention rows
For Q head i (1-indexed), g = H_q / H_kv = 4:
O_i = softmax( Q_i K_kv(i)^T / sqrt(128) ) V_kv(i)
boundaries: g = 1 -> MHA (kv(i) = i) g = H_q -> MQA (kv(i) = 1)
Within a group: Q_1 != Q_2 != Q_3 != Q_4 but K_1 = K_2 = K_3 = K_4.
Query-side diversity is kept; K/V diversity is reduced only 4x
(8 distinct K/V views instead of 1 in MQA, 32 in MHA).
3 Projection shapes (Llama-3-8B: d_model = 4096, H_q = 32, H_kv = 8, d_h = 128)
d_h = 4096/32 = 128 unchanged; Q and W_o untouched.
Query head i reads K/V head i // g (0-indexed).
2 x 4096 x 1024 FLOPs/token for K+V vs
4 Aligning K/V with Q: repeat_kv and the no-copy grouped form
expanded: each head x g = 4 (16 of 32 shown)
q head h -> kv head h // 4
def repeat_kv(k, g): # k: (B, T, H_kv, d_h)
k = k.expand(B, T, Hkv, g, d) # (B, T, Hkv, g, d) view, stride 0
return k.reshape(B, T, Hkv * g, d) # (B, T, H_q, d) <- materialises a copy
q = q.view(B, Hkv, g, d) # (B, 8, 4, 128) g rows per KV head
Each KV head is streamed from HBM ONCE and multiplied by g = 4
This is exactly why AI rises from 1 (MHA) to g.
Naive repeat_kv writes H_q x T x d_h x 2 B per layer per step for K, and the same again for V (2 x 32x128xT x 2 B),
re-inflating the cache to MHA size in HBM traffic. Fused kernels
(FlashAttention, vLLM paged-attn) index kv = h // g instead of copying.
5 Memory and arithmetic intensity: AI = H_q / H_kv
per token (all layers) = 2 . L . H_kv . d_h . S M_GQA = M_MHA . (H_kv / H_q) = M_MHA / g
Llama-3-8B shape: L=32, d_h=128, BF16 -> 2 . 32 . 128 . 2 B = 16 KiB per KV head
one layer, one decode token, S = 2
Bytes = 2 . H_kv . d_h . T . S = 4 . H_kv . d_h . T
(MHA 819 MB, MQA 25.6 MB); x32 layers = 6.55 GB
KV-read time lower bound @ 1.555 TB/s (toy, T=100K, B=1)
GQA is NOT only a VRAM saving: it cuts the bytes
moved per token by g, raising AI by g.
g = 4 still leaves AI = 4, ~50x below the A100
Faster decode = fewer bytes, not more FLOPS.
6 A100 40 GB, 7B FP16 weights (14 GB), 100K-token context (toy: L=32, d_h=64)
weights 14 GB + KV (B=1) 26 px per GB
MHA: 14 + 26.2 = 40.2 GB > 40 GB -> 100K context impossible even before runtime/workspace
GQA-8, 100K ctx: KV grows linearly with batch (20 px per GB)
max sequences @100K: MHA 0 GQA-16 1 GQA-8 3 GQA-4 6 MQA ~26
Same GPU, same weights: H_kv 32 -> 8 turns 'impossible' (40.2 GB) into 20.55 GB with room to batch.
Production schedulers must budget real sequence lengths, not 'batch = 32 and hope'.
7 Retrofit: MHA checkpoint -> GQA by mean-pooling heads (~5% of pretraining compute)
8 groups x 4 K heads each (35 px = 4 heads)
K_g = (1/n) sum_{i in g} K_i V_g = (1/n) sum_{i in g} V_i n = g = 4
(same for W_v); W_q, W_o, FFN, embeddings copied unchanged
Mean-pooling keeps the information of every original head
(unlike dropping heads), so the checkpoint starts close to its
old function and recovers quality in a short uptraining run.
GQA paper: mean pooling > picking one head > random init.
Uptrained GQA-8 ~ MHA quality at ~MQA speed.
Still needs a (small) training run and the same data/recipe discipline.
Cheaper than MHA -> MLA (low-rank factorisation + RoPE restructuring).
Mean-pooling all 32 heads gives an MQA init, but uptrained MQA is worse than GQA-8.
8 Choosing the ratio: quality vs cache, and what real models picked
SCHEMATIC trade-off (shape only, NOT measured values)
KV cache per token (fraction of MHA) ->
sweet spot: knee of the curve
H_kv 8 = most of MHA quality at 1/4 of the cache; 1 = fastest, weakest
Llama-2-7B/13B were still MHA; only 70B used GQA
- KV capacity bound (long ctx, many users): smaller H_kv
- TPOT bound (decode is KV-bandwidth bound): smaller H_kv
- quality critical: g = 4..8 (H_kv 8) is the usual answer
- tensor parallel degree P: want H_kv multiple of P
(8 KV heads = one per GPU on an 8-GPU node)
- have an MHA checkpoint: uptrain, do not retrain
H_kv < P forces K/V replication across GPUs
(MQA: 1 head copied on every GPU), so per-GPU
1. GQA: H_q Q heads, H_kv K/V heads, group size g = H_q/H_kv; Q head i reads K/V head i // g. g=1 is MHA, g=H_q is MQA.
2. Shapes: W_k, W_v 4096 x (H_kv*128); K, V cache (B, H_kv, T, 128); grouped scores (B, H_kv, g, T); output (B, 1, 4096).
3. Memory and bytes/token drop by g: toy 256 KiB -> 64 KiB/token (26.2 -> 6.55 GB at 100K); Llama-3-8B 512 -> 128 KiB/token (8K: 4 -> 1 GiB).
4. AI = g = 4 for GQA-8: 4x better than MHA but still ~50x below the A100 ridge (~200): decode stays memory-bound.
5. A100 40 GB with 14 GB weights: MHA @100K = 40.2 GB (OOM), GQA-8 = 20.55 GB. Retrofit: mean-pool K/V heads, ~5% extra compute.
Sources: Ainslie et al. 2023, GQA (arXiv 2305.13245); Shazeer 2019, MQA (arXiv 1911.02150); GPU ridge points: A100 312 TFLOPS / 1.555 TB/s, H100 SXM 989 TFLOPS / 3.35 TB/s
10 After GQA: what stacks on top of H_kv = H_Q / 4
Llama-3-8B shape (L = 32, H_Q = 32, H_kv = 8, d_h = 128). KiB per token, all layers. Bars to scale (1 px = 0.25 KiB). Full map: Beyond → KV cache SOTA map.
64 KiB · 8× less · 2 layers share one cache: attacks L
64 KiB · 8× less · 1 byte per element: attacks S
32 KiB · 16× less · terms multiply: ÷16 vs MHA
36 KiB · 14× less · retrofit: latent 512 + RoPE key 64
Key insight: GQA only shrinks H_kv. The other terms of M_KV = 2·L·B·T·H_kv·d_h·S are still free to attack, so GQA stacks with cross-layer sharing (L),
KV quantisation (S), eviction (T) and paging. TransMLA instead replaces the head-sharing scheme itself with a compressed latent.
